title: Capital-breach remedies escalate through four tiers, with the two extreme ones gated by an expedited Executive Vote
content:
The penalty Section builds a ladder rather than a single sanction. Financial penalties come first (A.3.2.2.7.2.1.1). If paying them would worsen the shortfall, forced token issuance (A.3.2.2.7.2.1.2). Independently, A.3.2.2.7.2.1.3 lets Core GovOps "impose whatever restrictions it deems necessary on the usage of the Allocation System Primitive," including limiting or prohibiting specific Instances, for any period it deems fit. And finally A.3.2.2.7.2.1.4: where "less extreme measures are not adequate to address the capital shortfall," Core GovOps may seek conservatorship, "in which case the Sky Core Facilitator takes direct control of the Prime Agent to maximize value for Sky and other Prime Agent stakeholders."

The ordering follows the reversibility of each step. A fine is refundable in effect; restrictions are lifted; dilution is permanent but bounded; conservatorship extinguishes the Agent's autonomy. Each tier is available only when the ones below are inadequate — the framework prefers the cheapest remedy that works.

The governance gate is what keeps the ladder legitimate. A.3.2.2.7.2.3.1 requires that "the extraordinary remedies of Prime Agent Conservatorship and Executor Accord Termination must always be escalated to a Sky Governance Executive Vote," and conservatorship specifically "requires immediate escalation to Sky Core Governance and requires an expedited Executive Vote." Operational bodies can fine, restrict and dilute on their own authority; only token holders can take an Agent over.

Disputes are symmetrically escalable: "In the event of a disagreement regarding the penalties for a violation of Risk Capital requirements, either party may escalate the matter to Sky Governance," resolved by Governance Poll after the Sky Core Facilitator gathers information from Core GovOps, Operational GovOps and the Agent (A.3.2.2.7.2.3.2). The enforcer is not the final arbiter of its own enforcement.

Notably, conservatorship's stated objective is to "maximize value for Sky **and other Prime Agent stakeholders**" — the takeover is framed as a receivership duty to the Agent's own creditors and owners, not purely as a Sky remedy.
description: Financial penalties, then forced token issuance, then Core GovOps restrictions on which Instances the Agent may use, then conservatorship where the Sky Core Facilitator takes direct control.
